title: Distilling reasoning traces with TRL's SFTTrainer

steps.title: The plan, and the pinned versions
steps.markdown: The docstring says what we're doing: fine-tune **Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct** (the student) on reasoning traces from **camel-ai/gsm8k_distilled** (MIT license), then measure GSM8K test accuracy before and after. The `pip install` line pins exact versions (TRL 1.16.0) so the script keeps working when libraries change. It needs a GPU; a free Colab T4 is enough.

steps.title: The knobs you'll actually change
steps.markdown: `N_TRAIN` is how many traces to learn from, `MAX_LENGTH` is the longest trace (in tokens) we keep, and `N_EVAL` is how many test problems we grade. The system prompt is the same `<think>`/`<answer>` instruction used in the GRPO labs, so the distilled model speaks the same format. The regular expressions find the thinking, the teacher's `\boxed{}` answer, our `<answer>` tag, and plain numbers.

steps.title: Rewriting a teacher trace into our format
steps.markdown: Each row in the dataset has a `problem`, a `reasoning_solution` (a `<think>` block followed by a written answer with `\boxed{}`), and a `boxed_answer_success` flag. `to_example` keeps only the thinking and the final number, and rebuilds the reply as `<think>…</think>` then `<answer>N</answer>`. It returns a **conversational prompt-completion** pair, a format TRL's `SFTTrainer` understands directly. Rows where the teacher's answer failed the check, or where something is missing, are marked `keep: False`.

steps.title: Filtering to traces that fit a T4
steps.markdown: Teacher traces can be long, and long sequences eat GPU memory. `build_train_set` shuffles the data (with a fixed seed, so you get the same subset every time), converts every row, drops failed ones, then drops any trace longer than `MAX_LENGTH` tokens once the chat template is applied. Finally it takes the first `N_TRAIN`. A side effect worth noticing: by keeping only shorter traces, we also teach the student a somewhat shorter thinking style.

steps.title: A fair grader
steps.markdown: The untrained student won't use our `<answer>` tag reliably, so grading only that tag would be unfair to the "before" run. `predicted_number` tries `<answer>` first, then `\boxed{}`, then simply the last number in the reply. Correctness is measured the same way before and after; the separate `format` score tells you whether the tags are being used.

steps.title: Evaluation: accuracy, format and length
steps.markdown: `evaluate` generates **greedy** answers (`do_sample=False`, always the most likely token) in batches of 16, so before and after are directly comparable. Padding goes on the *left* for generation, so every prompt ends right where the answer starts. For each reply it records: is the number right, did it use `</think>` and `<answer>`, and how many tokens it wrote (non-padding tokens). It returns the three averages plus the first reply to read.

steps.title: Test set and the "before" score
steps.markdown: We take the first 200 problems from the GSM8K **test** split; the traces came from the training split, so the student has never seen these. The gold answer is the number after `####`. We load the untouched student in float16, grade it, then delete it and free GPU memory before training.

steps.title: Training: SFTConfig, LoRA and SFTTrainer
steps.markdown:
This is plain next-token prediction on the teacher's text. Key settings:

- `completion_only_loss=True`: only the teacher's reply is graded, not the question.
- `per_device_train_batch_size=4` × `gradient_accumulation_steps=4` = 16 traces per update.
- `learning_rate=2e-4`: LoRA trains only small add-on matrices, so it tolerates a higher rate than full fine-tuning.
- `fp16=not bf16`: a T4 has no bfloat16, so we fall back to float16 mixed precision.
- `LoraConfig(target_modules="all-linear")` adds adapters to every linear layer.

We set padding back to the right before training, because `evaluate` switched it to the left.

steps.title: The "after" score and saving
steps.markdown: We grade the trained model (`trainer.model`, the student with its LoRA adapter) on the same 200 problems with the same settings, print a before/after table, and show the first answer so you can *read* what changed. Then we save the adapter, and upload it to the Hugging Face Hub if you set `HUB_MODEL_ID`.
